results.detail: Get Variables From Etl Varibles is no longer listed (correct: it sets User::GviaQueueId/MaasikimQueueId, DTSX:3283, which become the email from/to parties). Remaining items re-checked: Create ETL Process record only creates gen_etlprocess (gen_name, gen_etlname, gen_etlversion, gen_runinserver; it declares the queue variables as ReadOnly but never uses them, DTSX:40, 258-270); End ETL Process record updates gen_etlprocess (DTSX:903-911); Adding Error message 1 / 1 1 are Derived Columns on the Errors / Error outputs feeding ETL Warning 1 2 1 / 1 2 1 1 (paths); both ETL Warning scripts only create gen_etlprocesswarning (DTSX:4715-4727, 5487-5499) and differ only in AssemblyName. All are ETL plumbing.

Verified: [1] state 1, CreatedOn >= GETDATE()-7, ID match stripping leading zeros and spaces (PATINDEX('%[^0 ]%') both sides), Gen_existinfile = 1, gen_employerdepositdate <= fm.Gen_FundCreationDate, product pairs 1-1, 2-4, 3-2 (DTSX:6076-6112). [2] left join Gen_employers with AccountNumber = Gen_CorporateNumber; no existing-email check, no flag. [3] Check If To Send Mail main.cs:117-141 exactly as stated; deposit type 1 -> to Gvia, 2 -> to Maasikim, else nothing (main.cs:86-95). [4] email Create with regardingobjectid gen_employerenrolment, from/to activityparty on queue, directioncode true, then SendEmail IssueSend=true TrackingToken '' (main.cs:126-174); queue variables default empty (DTSX:20-25), ReadWrite in Get Variables (DTSX:3283); PostExecute throws when a ReadWrite variable is missing (DTSX:2656-2658); Success chain DTSX:7458-7459. Missing / imprecise: (a) unit 1 omits that the source query INNER JOINs Account on ee.gen_employersnumber = a.AccountId, so an enrolment with no (or no matching) employer account is never selected, including self-employed ones; (b) unit 4 says the queue ids come from 'gen_etlvariable' and that the step throws if a variable 'is not found in gen_etlvariable', but the query only reads rows WHERE gen_scope = 'global' OR gen_scope = ? with ? = System::PackageName (DTSX:2394-2398, ParameterMapping); a key stored under another scope also triggers the exception, and a duplicate key across those scopes makes Dictionary.Add throw in ProcessInputRow (case-insensitive dictionary) with the same Success-chain effect; (c) unit 4 lists the written email attributes but omits subject and description (the alert text, main.cs:133-134, 176-195).
